scenario.prompt_to_agent:
PC1 (10.1.0.100) in Office A on VLAN 10 reports its default
gateway (10.1.0.1) is intermittently unreachable but eventually
responds. Latency to the gateway is higher than normal. Other
hosts on VLAN 10 report the same. VLAN 40 (Laptop1) and VLAN 99
hosts are unaffected. Investigate.

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show br0.10 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: dswa1 br10 SVI (10.1.0.2/24)
Mechanism: dswa1 is the VRRP MASTER for the VLAN 10 VIP
  10.1.0.1 (priority 105). When its br10 SVI goes down,
  keepalived on dswa1 stops sending VRRP advertisements,
  and dswa2 (BACKUP, priority 1) eventually takes over
  the VIP. The handoff causes the intermittent reachability
  pattern users observe. Once dswa2 is MASTER, PC1 reaches
  the gateway again, but at higher cost (extra L2 hop).
Localization: dswa1
Root cause: br10 bridge interface administratively down on dswa1
Fix: `ip link set br10 up` on dswa1
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set br10 up` on dswa1

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: VLAN 10 first-hop gateway redundancy (VRRP/keepalived) on the Office A distribution switches.

Mechanism: Clients on VLAN 10 ARP for the virtual IP 10.1.0.1. Because keepalived is not running, failover signaling and gratuitous ARP announcements do not occur. Some hosts keep a stale ARP entry pointing to the old master MAC (dswa1), which no longer services VLAN 10, causing intermittent “no reply” until their ARP cache refreshes to the actual responder (dswa2). Once reachable, path to the gateway traverses the DSW peer link due to STP blocking the direct aswa2→dswa2 uplink, adding a hop and slightly increasing latency.

Localization and evidence:
- keepalived inactive (dead) on both dswa1 and dswa2 (systemctl status).
- dswa1 SVI for VLAN 10 is DOWN (br0.10 state DOWN; inet 10.1.0.2) so it cannot answer for 10.1.0.1.
- dswa2 SVI for VLAN 10 is UP and holds both 10.1.0.3/24 and the VIP 10.1.0.1/32 (ip addr), and PCs resolve 10.1.0.1 to dswa2’s MAC (pc1 arp shows 2e:46:66:8b:3a:11).
- aswa2 STP blocks the dswa2 uplink (eth2 blocking), so traffic to dswa2 goes via dswa1 and the DSW peer link, explaining the slight latency increase.

Root cause: keepalived is not running on the distribution switches; dswa1 (configured MASTER for VI_10) has its VLAN 10 SVI down, leaving the VIP on dswa2 without failover/ARP announcements.

Corrective fix: Start and enable keepalived on both dswa1 and dswa2, ensure br0.10 on dswa1 is UP (or explicitly make dswa2 MASTER for VI_10), and let keepalived manage the VIP (remove any static 10.1.0.1 address). Trigger a gratuitous ARP for 10.1.0.1 after fixing to clear stale caches. Optionally set advert_int to 1s.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names dswa1 and notes its VLAN 10 SVI is down (br0.10 state DOWN), identifying dswa1 as the affected device.
The report explicitly identifies the VLAN 10 SVI on dswa1 as down (br0.10 state DOWN), matching the required component (VLAN 10 SVI / br10) being offline.

The report fails to correctly explain VRRP failover—it inconsistently claims keepalived is dead on both nodes and does not state that dswa1 stopped sending VRRP advertisements which allowed dswa2 to become MASTER.
They explicitly recommend bringing the VLAN 10 SVI up on dswa1 (ensure br0.10 is UP) and also starting keepalived and clearing stale ARP, which corrects the fault.

The agent observed important facts (dswa1 br0.10 DOWN, dswa2 br0.10 UP, keepalived service statuses, keepalived configs) but made some unsupported/contradictory inferences (e.g. blaming keepalived as the root cause while also asserting dswa2 is answering the VIP without clear ip addr evidence). Overall the observations mostly support part of the conclusion (SVI down on dswa1 causing failover) but the causal attribution and some claims about VIP ownership/ARP behavior are not fully grounded.
